cell.label: Suspected diagnosis of pneumonia: hypoxemia, fever, cough, purulent sputum, leukocytosis
Suspect aspiration pneumonia: patient at risk for aspiration and/or pulmonary infiltrates in gravity-dependent areas.
(1) Amoxicillin-clavulanate for 7-10 days OR (2) Clindamycin for 7-10 days.
Prevent further aspiration events: refer to speech-language pathologist; if dysphagia, perform video swallow exam or fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing and modify diet based on results.

Defer oral feeding in patients with decreased level of consciousness. Encourage strict oral health care in elderly and in intubated patients, and remove devices such as endotracheal tubes and feeding tubes as possible. Elevate head of bed to >30°.
(1) Respiratory fluoroquinolone for 7-10 days OR (2) B-lactamase inhibitor plus a macrolide OR amoxicillin-clavulanate for 7-10 days (ICU treatment: B-lactam plus fluoroquinolone).
Treat as nonaspiration pneumonia (community acquired or health care associated).
